messages:
anya: quick q — when we talked about adding a 'scope' to runtime flags, i sketched an API change. ran a couple of integration tests and saw routing fallbacks ignore cohort-level overrides. anyone else see this?

mike: @anya can you paste the payload you sent? my guess is we might be treating scope as a soft filter vs. an override.

anya: here’s the minimal body i used:
```json
{
  "flag_key": "route_by_cost",
  "value": { "percent": 10 },
  "scope": { "type": "cohort", "id": "beta-accounts" }
}
```
expectation: requests from cohort get the 10% ballot. observed: cohort requests sometimes hit default route, other times the cohort override applied for a different feature flag (possible cache key collision?) :eyes:

sarah: hmm could be caching. we recently changed the cache key to include model+route only, removed flag scope to reduce cardinality. that would explain collisions.

jordan: if cache keys don't include scope, prefix/KV cache could return a tokenized state that was served under default flags — leading to incorrect routing. we need to decide: add scope back to key or canonicalize overrides into the request context before caching.

mike: +1 to canonicalize before caching, that keeps cache size down if we can normalize scope values. but how do we canonicalize cohorts? thousands of cohorts = explosion.

anya: proposal: at edge we normalize scope into a `scope_hash` computed from (type,id) and only include the hash in keys. hash namespace limited to active cohorts for routing to avoid explosion.

sarah: that could work. we need telemetry to know how often scope changes map to different behavior. can we add a telemetry tag on cache hits that reports whether scope_hash matched and whether fallback decision differed?

ops-bot: deploy-check: no rollout in progress for routing-service. current stable: v3.12.3.

jordan: telemetry idea: emit metric `routing.cache_scope_mismatch` with labels: flag_key, scope_type, scope_present(true/false). keep it high-cardinality-safe by sampling 1% by default and 100% when throttled count spikes.

mike: i like sampled baseline + spike capture. need to wire into console dashboard too so PMs can watch during rollout. UX note: console should show per-flag "scope coverage" — percent of requests with a scope value vs default.

anya: implementation plan: (1) edge computes scope_hash; (2) runtime normalizes request context to include scope_hash before cache key; (3) add routing telemetry hooks; (4) canary rollout with 5% of traffic to verify.

sarah: for canary, prefer cohort-based canary (specific orgs) rather than random 5% — better for debugging. also add dry-run mode where we log what would have happened without applying scope to cache.

mike: question on API shape: do we want `scope` at top-level of flag payload or nested under `targeting`? small bikeshed but affects SDKs.

anya: leaning top-level — simpler for runtime and for backwards compat. SDKs can treat `scope` as optional top-level field.

jordan: ok. I'll draft the change request and a short rollback plan (remove scope from cache key, revert sampling). who volunteers to own telemetry dashboard?

mike: i can mock the dashboard tiles (cache mismatch rate + per-flag scope coverage), will share a preview.

sarah: i'll add the dry-run hook and integration tests for key collisions.

anya: i'll own the API docs + SDK note. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: leaving a tiny note — add a feature-flagged runtime toggle so ops can flip scope gating off quickly if we see perf regressions.

jordan: good call. include a short playbook line: "if routing latency increases > 30ms p95 after canary, set runtime.toggle.scope_hashing=false and rollback canary".

ops-bot: note: scheduled config change window at 02:00 UTC tonight. ensure all changes are marked NO ROLLBACK during critical window.

anya: ack. will avoid merging into prod branch until after the window.

mike: cheers — will post the dashboard preview link shortly.
